exchange_rate.budget_in_krw: US$1,000 pp = about 1,340,000 KRW; US$3,000 total = about 4,020,000 KRW
exchange_rate.note: Won has strengthened ~5.6% over 12 months, so dollar budgets buy a bit less than 2025 guides suggest. Use 1,340 for planning; a 1,300-1,380 band is a reasonable stress test.

places.name: Incheon International Airport Terminal 1
places.summary: Arrival and departure airport. Air Premia is understood to operate from T1 (confirm on e-ticket; Asiana moved to T2 on Jan 14 2026, Air Busan and Air Seoul also moved to T2 in 2025).
places.why: Dawn arrival at 05:15 Sat Oct 17 and departure 21:55 Sun Oct 25.
places.time_needed: Arrival: allow 45-75 min for immigration + bags before heading into Seoul. Departure: be at the airport by ~19:00 (3h before).
places.hours: 24h; AREX Express first train from T1 05:23 (T2 05:15); all-stop trains from ~05:20
places.tips: Darakhyu capsule hotel (landside, transportation center of each terminal) rents rooms by the block: roughly 30,000-40,000 KRW for 3 hours or 60,000-80,000 KRW overnight per room (Wikivoyage snapshot, prices not 2026-verified). Spa on Air (T1 B1 sauna) listed at ~15,000 KRW overnight/27,000 private room, but its 2026 operating status could not be confirmed.

places.name: Seoul Station (KTX, AREX, City Airport Terminal)
places.summary: Main KTX hub for Gyeongbu (Busan, Gyeongju) and Gangneung lines; AREX terminus; T-Luggage storage counter.
places.why: Most of the trip's rail legs start or end here.
places.tips: City Airport Terminal check-in (B2) participating airlines per Sep 2026 source: Korean Air, Asiana, Jeju Air, Jin Air, T'way, Eastar Jet, Air Seoul. Air Premia is NOT on the list, so the travelers cannot check bags in at Seoul Station.

places.name: Gyeongju Station (formerly Singyeongju)
places.summary: KTX station for Gyeongju on the Gyeongbu HSR, Donghae Line and Jungang Line; booking sites may now list it as 'Gyeongju (경주)' rather than 'Singyeongju'. ~20-30 min by bus/taxi to the historic center.
places.why: Gateway to Gyeongju and junction for Busan-Bujeon and Gangneung east-coast trains.
places.tips: Search for both '경주' and 'Singyeongju' in apps. Taxi to Hwangnidan-gil roughly 20,000-25,000 KRW (estimate).

transport.booking: Korail+ app or korail.com English site; tickets open 2 months ahead at 07:00 (from Oct 1 2026)
transport.notes: Fare cut from 59,800 on Sep 1 2026 when SRT merged into KTX. Standing/unreserved 46,200. Suseo station departures (former SRT) are now also KTX and searchable in the same app; useful if Seoul Station sells out.
Fastest Gyeongju-Busan link; Busan Station is convenient for Nampo/Jung-gu and Haeundae via subway.
KTX-Eum 12,500; ITX-Maeum 10,100; Mugunghwa 6,800. Bujeon is in central Busan (Seomyeon area); Busan Station is better if staying in Nampo/Jung-gu.

transport.frequency: ~14/day from Seoul Station (first 05:06, last 22:14); more from Cheongnyangni
transport.notes: Cheongnyangni-Gangneung 26,000. The Sep 2026 10% cut does not appear to have changed this fare (still 27,600 in the Oct 7-13 2026 timetable). Weekend trains in foliage season sell out fast.

transport.frequency: Only 4-5/day from Seoul Station (06:44-18:36); most Jeonju trains run from Yongsan, ~1-2/hour
transport.notes: One web summary quoted 48,200 for Yongsan-Jeonju; that looks like a mismatch (likely another route/class). 31,900 is from the Oct 7-13 2026 timetable; check Korail+ for Yongsan departures.
ITX-Maeum 21,100. Andong station is ~10-15 min from downtown; Hahoe Village is ~40-50 min by bus/taxi.

transport.mode: KTX-Eum (Donghae Line via Gyeongju, Pohang, Yeongdeok, Uljin, Samcheok, Donghae, Jeongdongjin)
transport.booking: Korail+ / korail.com; book early, only ~3 trains
transport.notes: Scenic coastal line opened Dec 30 2024. Gangneung->Bujeon departures roughly 09:36ish-pattern trains (752/754/756 at 09:36, 14:56, 18:35 from Gangneung).
ITX-Maeum fare 24,800. Lets you link Gangneung and Gyeongju without returning to Seoul.

transport.from: Seoul Express Bus Terminal (Gangnam) or Dong Seoul Terminal
transport.duration: ~2h10m-2h40m (Seoul-Yangyang Expressway; traffic on autumn weekends can add 1h+)
transport.frequency: Very frequent (every 15-40 min) from both terminals
transport.booking: Kobus (express) / Bustago & T-money Bus apps; foreign cards often fail in apps, buy at terminal kiosks/counters or via Klook/Trip.com
transport.notes: ESTIMATE. Bus fare caps rose 9% on Oct 1 2026; route-specific new fares were not published. Pre-increase roughly 19,000 regular / 24,000 premium (우등) / ~30,000 premium-plus; expect ~21,000 / ~26,000 / ~33,000 now. Check displayed fare.

transport.booking: Buy at Gangneung Intercity Bus Terminal or app
transport.notes: ESTIMATE after the Oct 1 2026 9% cap increase (was roughly 7,000-8,000).

transport.frequency: Every ~30-40 min; first from T1 05:23, from T2 05:15
transport.booking: Ticket machines/counter at airport; Klook/Trip.com discount vouchers common
transport.notes: Regular adult fare reported as 13,000 by Wikivoyage, 11,000 when discounted (Korean source). Treat as 11,000-13,000. After a 05:15 landing, expect to reach the platform ~06:00-06:30.
Fare range 4,150-5,050 depending on terminal and destination. Cheapest; fine with carry-on, crowded with big suitcases later in the morning.

transport.to: Central Seoul (Myeongdong, Gwanghwamun, Jongno, Gangnam hotels)
transport.frequency: First departures ~05:30-06:00 on major routes, then every 15-30 min
transport.booking: Ticket counters/kiosks in arrivals; card or cash
transport.notes: Wikivoyage lists 15,000; recent fares on most Seoul limousine routes are ~17,000-18,000. Drops near many hotels, good with luggage.

transport.mode: Taxi (regular / deluxe / Kakao T or Uber)
transport.booking: Taxi rank outside arrivals; Kakao T / k.ride / Uber also work
transport.notes: Regular taxi ~65,000-80,000 KRW total including highway tolls (~7,000); deluxe/black ~90,000-110,000. Split by 3 = ~22,000-27,000 pp, competitive with the express train and door-to-door with luggage at 6 a.m. Night surcharge applies before 04:00 only.

transport.frequency: Very frequent (every few minutes in daytime)
transport.booking: Airline sites (Korean Air, Asiana, Jeju Air, Jin Air, T'way, Air Seoul, Eastar) or Trip.com
transport.notes: TYPICAL RANGE, not 2026-verified: ~30,000-120,000 KRW one-way incl. taxes; LCC midweek low end, Friday/Sunday afternoons high. Not recommended for an 8-night first trip unless Jeju is a priority.

prices_krw_adult.saver_discount: About 10,000-15,000 KRW off per person for 2-5 travelling together

korail_pass.price_conflicts: Shopback (Aug 2026) lists 131k/186k/234k/275k; koreaexperience lists 4-day 213k, consecutive 3-day 175k, 5-day 225k; Trazy/haniseoul (Mar 2026) in USD 87.50 (2-day) to 188 (5-day). Prices vary by reseller.
korail_pass.coverage: KTX, KTX-Sancheon, KTX-Eum, ITX, Mugunghwa, tourist trains. Historically excluded SRT; after the Sep 1 2026 merger nobody has officially said whether the pass now covers ex-SRT (Suseo) trains.
korail_pass.limits: Max 2 reserved seats per day; standard class; buy online at least a day ahead; foreigners only.
korail_pass.verdict: Not worth it. A likely 3-4 leg plan (Seoul->Gyeongju 44,500 + Gyeongju->Busan 10,100 + Busan->Seoul 54,400, optionally Seoul<->Gangneung 55,200 round trip) costs ~109,000-164,000 KRW pp, spread over 3-5 different days, versus 186,000-275,000 for a pass. Point-to-point tickets win after the Sep 2026 fare cut.

tips: KTX/SRT merged on Sep 1 2026: SRT brand is gone (trains now 'KTX-Sancheon'), fares cut ~10% on high-speed routes (Seoul-Busan 59,800 -> 54,400), and Seoul, Yongsan and Suseo departures are all searchable in one app, Korail+ (renamed Korail Talk). The SRT app/website closed Aug 31 2026.

From Oct 1 2026 Korail tickets go on sale 2 months before departure at 07:00 (was 1 month). As of Oct 6 every train for Oct 17-25 is already bookable: buy now, especially Saturday/Sunday trains and the 3-a-day Donghae Line KTX-Eum.

Foreigners: book on korail.com (English 'foreigner' reservation) or Korail+ app in English. Overseas cards sometimes fail at 3-D Secure or ask for a Korean phone number; fall back to korail.com desktop, station ticket counters/machines, or resellers (Trip.com, Klook, 12Go, LACHA) that accept foreign cards for a small markup. Korail says Visa/Master/UnionPay plus WeChat/Alipay support is being developed.
Korail+ lets you cancel free within 10 minutes of purchase; after that small fees apply, rising close to departure.
Rail fares for the likely itinerary per person: Seoul->Gyeongju 44,500 + Gyeongju->Busan 10,100 + Busan->Seoul 54,400 = 109,000 KRW (~US$81). For 3 people ~327,000 KRW (~US$244).

Dawn arrival (05:15 Sat Oct 17): booking the night of Oct 16 so the room is ready at ~07:00 is the reliable option for 3 jet-lagged adults. Without it, ask the hotel for luggage drop + early check-in (rarely guaranteed before 12:00-15:00 on a Saturday).

Getting into Seoul at dawn: a taxi (~65,000-80,000 total incl. tolls, ~US$17-20 each) is door-to-door and as cheap as 3 AREX Express tickets plus a subway/taxi transfer. AREX all-stop (~4,750) is the budget option.
Air Premia is understood to use Incheon Terminal 1. Confirm on the e-ticket/app the week of travel, since several carriers changed terminals in 2025-2026.

Last day (21:55 departure Sun Oct 25): Air Premia does not participate in Seoul Station City Airport Terminal check-in, so bags travel with you. Leave bags at the hotel (free) and pick up, or use T-Luggage lockers/counters (Seoul Station, Myeongdong, Hongdae, Jongno 3-ga, Jamsil, Suseo, Gimpo; 09:00-22:00; ~6,000-13,000 KRW per large bag). Leave central Seoul by ~17:30 to be at T1 by ~19:00.

T-Luggage also delivers bags from Seoul stations to Incheon airport (listed as T2) for 20,000 KRW weekday / 29,000 KRW weekend per bag; book a day ahead (cancellations after 18:00 the day before are non-refundable). Check if T1 delivery is offered for Air Premia.
Busan luggage: ZimCarry (Busan Station based, 1544-8215) offers storage, hotel/station delivery and KTX luggage shipping; handy on the Busan travel day.

Transit cards: a T-money card (3,000-5,000 KRW at convenience stores) works on subways, buses and many taxis nationwide (Seoul, Busan, Gyeongju, Gangneung). WOWPASS is a prepaid debit card with built-in T-money, top-up by foreign card or cash machine; good for foreigners whose cards fail in Korean apps. Top up T-money with cash only at machines/convenience stores.

Seoul subway base fare is 1,550 KRW (card) since mid-2025; buses ~1,500. Seoul's Climate Card tourist pass (unlimited Seoul subway/bus, roughly 1-day 5,000 to 7-day 20,000 KRW plus card) only pays off on heavy-transit Seoul days and does not cover AREX to Incheon; T-money/WOWPASS is simpler for this itinerary.
Foreign credit cards (Visa/Mastercard; Amex less so) are accepted almost everywhere, including taxis and markets; carry some cash for street food and small market stalls.
Taxis: Kakao T accepts foreign phone numbers and overseas cards; Kakao's English app k.ride and Uber also work in Seoul and Busan. Seoul taxi base fare is 4,800 KRW.
Maps: use Naver Map (English UI) or Kakao Map for walking/transit directions; Google Maps lacks walking/driving directions in Korea. Papago for translation (camera mode for menus).
Restaurant reservations: CatchTable Global (English, foreign phone and card OK) is the main way to book omakase/fine dining as a foreigner; Naver booking often needs a Korean number.

eSIM/data: get a tourist eSIM (KT/SKT/LG U+ or Airalo-type, roughly 25,000-45,000 KRW for 8-10 days unlimited) or a physical tourist SIM with a Korean number if you want Kakao T/CatchTable verification and delivery apps.

Entry: US citizens are K-ETA-exempt through Dec 31 2026, so no K-ETA is needed for Oct 17. Instead each traveler must file the free Korea e-Arrival Card online (e-arrivalcard.go.kr) within 3 days before arrival (paper cards were replaced from Jan 1 2026). Optional: a K-ETA (10,000 KRW, valid 3 years, k-eta.go.kr only) replaces the e-Arrival Card and covers future 2027+ trips.
Tipping is not customary in Korea (restaurants, taxis, hotels); service charges are included at upscale hotels.

Tax refunds: look for 'Tax Free' stores; immediate refund at the register for purchases of 15,000-under 1,000,000 KRW per receipt (up to ~5,000,000 KRW total per trip), show passport. Larger purchases: refund kiosks at Incheon before security.
No public holidays fall on Oct 17-25 2026 (Chuseok was Sep 24-26; Hangul Day Oct 9), but autumn foliage weekends make Saturday/Sunday trains and buses to Gangneung/Sokcho and Gyeongju busy.
warnings: Express and intercity bus fare caps rose 9% on Oct 1 2026; route-level fares (Seoul-Sokcho, Gangneung-Sokcho) were not yet published anywhere I could find, so the bus prices here are estimates.
Korail Pass validity on ex-SRT (Suseo) trains after the Sep 2026 merger is officially unclarified; another reason to skip the pass.
Overseas cards can be rejected at 3-D Secure on Korail+; try korail.com on desktop or buy at the station if the app fails.
Singyeongju station now appears as 'Gyeongju (경주)' in some timetables/booking screens; don't confuse it with the old downtown Gyeongju station (closed 2021).

Car rental is not recommended: an International Driving Permit (1949 Geneva type, from AAA) plus US license and passport are required, drivers usually 21+ with 1+ year experience, Seoul traffic and parking are hard, and speed cameras are everywhere. The rail network covers every planned leg. A one-day rental in Gyeongju or Gangneung/Sokcho is the only case worth considering.
Seoul Station City Airport Terminal check-in excludes Air Premia; do not plan an early bag drop there.
Darakhyu/Spa on Air prices and Spa on Air's current operating status are from older snapshots and could not be confirmed for 2026.
Domestic flight prices are typical ranges, not live 2026 fares.
